A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaves are undivided single blades)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology

    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (the leaf tip tapers gradually to a distinct point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (the leaf base tapers inward toward the petiole attachment)

    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible and prominent, spaced relatively evenly along the midrib

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the stem appears thin, green, and flexible)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the stem surface appears smooth)

    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no ridges or lenticels are apparent on the stem surface)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf bases in any image)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed

F. Notes: The seedling displays distinct pinnate venation with prominent secondary veins that curve toward the leaf margin. Several leaves exhibit small, irregular brown spots and minor edge damage. A pink identification tag is visible near the base of the plant in multiple images.
